correctness.rationale: The unit-sphere Voronoi partition has 12 regular pentagonal icosahedral and 20 regular triangular dodecahedral cells with five/three sides; their common spherical circumradius gives r=sqrt((5+2sqrt(5))/15). For cap radii at most the cell circumradius, exterior-halfplane segments are disjoint; spherical integration yields the explicit B and hence both survival CDFs. The difference H increases from zero on (r,c_I) by the positive difference of clipped-angle derivatives; on (c_I,c_D) it has decreasing derivative and positive endpoints; on (c_D,1) it equals 4(1-t). The boundary quadratic constant is from the exact second derivative. Direct coordinate-generated widths at seven thresholds, one 1999-point grid, and published second-moment checks corroborate but do not prove these statements.

originality.rationale: The inspected literature gives general cap calculations or general polyhedral normal-fan width densities and moments of individual Platonic solids. An abstract normal-fan formula alone does not establish this explicit golden-dual pair of CDFs, their equal circumradius support identity, nor their strictly positive survival difference for every interior threshold. The analytic comparison is not implied by any finite family of width moments. Targeted published-finding corpus searches identified the nearest published mathematical records but no equivalent all-threshold ordering statement. Potential unindexed earlier special cases are a residual historical priority risk.
residual_risks: Full text of the published mathematical-record results was not accessible through the available published-finding corpus index, so those claims were compared using available abstracts/summaries only.
Unindexed older treatment of golden-polyhedron widths or equivalent spherical cap unions might already include the special case.
The explicit distributions specialize known general normal-fan machinery; originality chiefly concerns their strict stochastic comparison.

value.rationale: The regular icosahedron and dodecahedron are the natural dual Platonic pair. The normalized support endpoints coincide, so endpoint extrema and a few moments do not predict whether one entire direction-width distribution dominates the other. The proof resolves competing cap multiplicity and clipping terms at every threshold, giving meaningful exact distributional comparison and distinct quantitative endpoint laws.
